title: hotfix: handle edge case in SLO enforcer regional failover path
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: During an incident on 2025-11-05 we observed the SLO enforcer's regional failover path enter a slow-retry loop when downstream region metadata returned a 202 / deferred status for certain warmup requests. This caused cascading backpressure and ineffective load-shedding decisions in the enforcer, resulting in elevated P99 latency for a small subset of customers. This PR fixes the edge case and adds defensive checks and unit/integration coverage.

Summary of changes: - Detect deferred/warmup responses from regional-capacity API and treat them as transient but not-ready: introduce a short backoff + fast-fail heuristic so traffic can immediately route to the next healthy region. - Add a quorum check to avoid flipping routing decision on single noisy signals. - Fix a race in the in-memory region-state cache that could return stale timestamps during rapid failover. - Add unit tests and an integration test that simulates multi-region partial warmup.

Testing & validation: - Unit test coverage added for the new heuristic and cache race guard. - Integration test in perf-canary simulates a 202-deferred scenario and verifies traffic reroutes within expected window and SLOs remain within target. - Ran full CI (lint, unit, integration, e2e) locally and on CI; initial integration flakiness was addressed by tightening timeouts and adding a small deterministic sleep in the test harness.

Checklist: - [x] Reproduced the failure locally and in staging. - [x] Added tests that reproduce and prevent regression. - [x] Verified no behavioural change for normal successful regional responses. - [x] Documented the heuristic in ops runbook (docs/ops/slo-enforcer.md).

Impacted areas: SLO enforcer (service/slo-enforcer), regional routing logic (pkg/routing), region state cache (pkg/regioncache), ops docs.

Release notes: Hotfix: fix regional failover edge case where deferred/warmup responses could cause prolonged backoff and elevated tail latency; adds faster failover heuristic and stability guards.

Merge: squash merge to main after approvals and CI green.
